en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa Dhammapaccanīya (2), Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (1) 7.22.
Sanidassanattika (The Triplet on the Visible)
Dependent on a state that is non-internal, non-visible, and impinging, there arises a state that is non-internal, non-visible, and impinging by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is non-internal, non-visible, and impinging, there arises a state that is non-internal, non-visible, and non-impinging by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is non-internal, non-visible, and impinging... [there arises] a state that is non-internal, non-visible, and non-impinging... [by way of root condition].

A state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is non-visible and impinging, there arise states that are both non-visible and impinging and non-visible and non-impinging, by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is non-visible and impinging, there arise states that are non-visible and non-impinging, by way of root condition.

By way of root condition: dependent on a state that is non-visible and impinging, there arise states that are both non-visible and impinging and non-visible and non-impinging by way of root condition;
dependent on a state that is non-visible and non-impinging, there arises a state that is non-visible and non-impinging by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not visible and impinging, a state that is not visible and impinging arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not visible and impinging, a state that is not visible and non-impinging arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not visible and impinging, a state that is not visible and impinging... [arises].
And through the condition of cause, phenomena that are non-visible and non-reactive arise.
Dependent on a phenomenon that is non-visible and with-reactive, phenomena that are both non-visible and with-reactive and non-visible and non-reactive arise through the condition of cause.
Dependent on a phenomenon that is non-visible and with-reactive, phenomena that are both non-visible and with-reactive and non-visible and non-reactive [arise]...
And states arise with the root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is non-visible and non-reacting, a state that is non-visible and non-reacting arises with the root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is non-visible and non-reacting, a state that is non-visible but reacting arises with the root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither visible nor impinging, a state that is neither visible nor impinging arises by way of root condition... Six.
Dependent on a state that is both not invisible and impinging and neither visible nor impinging, a state that is not invisible and impinging arises by way of root condition... Six.
Dependent on a state that is both not invisible and impinging and neither visible nor impinging, a state that is not invisible and impinging arises by way of root condition... Six. (Abbreviated.)
In the cause condition, thirty; in the object condition, nine ... pe ... in the mutuality condition, twenty-five ... pe ... in the non-disappearance condition, thirty.

(Just as it was calculated in the wholesome triad—namely, the section on co-nascence, the section on conditions, the section on support, the section on association, the section on conjunction, and the section on inquiry—so too should it be calculated here.)
